title: ICD implant (implantable defibrillator)
what: A small device is placed under the skin below the collarbone, and leads are passed through a vein to the heart. If the rhythm becomes dangerous, the device restores it, sometimes with a shock.
why: For a high risk of dangerous heart rhythms, for example after cardiac arrest or with a very weak heart.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours, with 1 to 3 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies, including to antibiotics and antiseptics
Which hand you write with. The device usually goes on the other side

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and a heart ultrasound. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Shower the day before. Sometimes you are asked to shave your chest.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that open at the front, your medicines, and a charger.

bring: Documents and a list of your medicines
Things for a 1 to 3 day hospital stay
steps: An IV line is placed, and you get a sedative
The skin below the collarbone is numbed with a shot
The doctor makes a small cut and passes the leads through a vein to the heart
The leads are connected to the device
The device is placed under the skin, and the cut is stitched
The device is tested, sometimes under brief anesthesia
feel: Pressure and tugging during the surgery
Pain at the cut for a few days. You will get painkillers
after: For a few weeks, do not raise the arm on the device side above your shoulder
No heavy lifting for about a month
You will get a device card. Carry it with you
Device checks on your doctor's schedule
Your doctor will explain about magnets, phones, and airport scanners
red_flags: The device gave a shock and you feel unwell, or several shocks in a row: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness, pus, or swelling over the device
Severe shortness of breath or fainting: call emergency services

faq.q: What will I feel if the device gives a shock?
faq.a: A strong jolt in the chest for a moment. If it is one shock and you feel fine, tell your doctor. If you feel unwell, call emergency services.

faq.q: Can I drive with the device?
faq.a: There may be limits, especially at first and after shocks. Your doctor will say for how long.

reminders.text: Defibrillator implant tomorrow. Take a shower, and pack your documents and things. Eat only until the time the clinic gave you.
